liheapIncomeLimits.description: 60% of Georgia state median income, by household size
liheapIncomeLimits.needsVerification: Third-party source. Sizes 1 and 4 come from the source; others derived with standard SMI ratios. Confirm with Georgia DFCS before the demo.

programs.name: Georgia Power Income-Qualified Discount
programs.whoQualifies: Household income at or below 200% of the federal poverty level AND someone is 65+, receives SSI or SSDI, or has a Section 8 voucher.
programs.howToApply: Use the online pre-qualifier at georgiapower.com, or call Georgia Power customer service.
checklist: Your Georgia Power account number (top of your bill)
Proof of age (driver's license or state ID), OR your SSI/SSDI award letter, OR your Section 8 voucher
Proof of household income (Social Security statement, pension statement, or recent pay stubs)

programs.name: LIHEAP (heating, cooling and crisis help)
programs.value: $400–$810 per season, paid directly to Georgia Power
programs.whoQualifies: Household income at or below 60% of Georgia's state median income. Funding is first come, first served each season.
programs.howToApply: Book an appointment with your county's community action agency. Seniors 65+ and homebound residents often get early access.
checklist: Photo ID for the person applying
Social Security cards (or numbers) for everyone in the household
Proof of income for everyone in the household for the last 30 days
Your most recent Georgia Power bill
Your heating bill, if heat comes from a different company

programs.name: Georgia Power EASE (free home energy upgrades)
programs.value: Free insulation, air sealing and HVAC service, up to $5,000
programs.renterNote: Renters need written consent from their landlord.
programs.whoQualifies: Household income at or below 300% of the federal poverty level. Renters need landlord consent.
programs.howToApply: Apply online, then schedule a free home assessment.
checklist: If you rent: your landlord's written consent
A time you can be home for the assessment

programs.name: Weatherization Assistance Program
programs.value: Free upgrades based on a home energy audit
programs.renterNote: Renters usually need the landlord's permission.
programs.whoQualifies: Household income at or below 200% of the federal poverty level. Priority for seniors, people with disabilities and families with children.
programs.howToApply: Contact your local weatherization agency (administered with GEFA).
checklist: Proof of income for everyone in the household
Proof you own the home, or your landlord's permission

programs.name: Project SHARE (emergency energy help)
programs.whoQualifies: Decided case by case for households in crisis, such as a past-due bill or a shutoff notice.
programs.howToApply: Visit or call your local Salvation Army office.
checklist: Your past-due bill or shutoff notice
